title: Work Schedules — Hours, Shifts, and Availability
description: Learn to talk about work hours, shifts, and when you are available to work
objectives: Ask and answer questions about work hours
Say when you are available and when you are not
Understand words like shift, overtime, full-time, and part-time
Use time prepositions: on, at, from...to, until

phrases: What are the hours for this job?
I can work from [7 AM] to [4 PM]
Do you offer full-time or part-time work?
What shift would I be working?
target_language.grammar_pattern:
AVAILABILITY with CAN and AVAILABLE
  I can work weekdays. → I'm available on weekdays.
  I can't work nights. → I'm not available for the night shift.

TIME PREPOSITIONS for schedules
  on + days: I work on Mondays. / I'm off on Sundays.
  at + time: I start at 7 AM. / The shift ends at 3 PM.
  from...to: I work from 8 to 5. / The store is open from 9 to 9.
  until: I can work until 6 PM. / The shift runs until midnight.

FULL-TIME vs PART-TIME
  Full-time = usually 40 hours per week.
  Part-time = fewer than 40 hours per week.

grammar_patterns.label: Availability with CAN
grammar_patterns.pattern: I can / I can't work + [time / day]
examples: I can work Monday through Friday.
I can work the morning shift.
I can't work on Sundays.
Can you work overtime?

grammar_patterns.label: Prepositions: ON, AT, FROM...TO
examples: I work on weekdays from 8 AM to 4 PM.
The night shift starts at 10 PM.
I'm available from Monday to Friday.
I work until 6 PM on Thursdays.

grammar_patterns.label: Asking about schedule
grammar_patterns.pattern: What are the hours? / What shift...? / Is ... available?
examples: What are the hours for this position?
What shift would I be working?
Is overtime available at this job?
Do you offer full-time or part-time work?

story.context: Ahmed has an interview at a warehouse. The hiring manager, Tom, asks about Ahmed's availability and explains the schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: Thanks for coming in, Ahmed. Before we talk about the job, let me ask — what hours can you work?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: I can work any days, Monday to Saturday. I prefer morning or daytime shifts.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: Good. This position is full-time, Monday through Friday. The shift is from 6 AM to 2:30 PM. Does that work for you?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: Yes, that works well. I can start at 6 AM. What time does the shift end — is it at 2:30 every day?

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: Yes, always at 2:30. Sometimes we offer overtime on Saturdays — would you be available for that?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: Yes, I'm available on Saturdays too. Is overtime common here?

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: Maybe one or two Saturdays a month. It's always optional, never required. Are you also available for some Sundays if we're very busy?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: I'm not available on Sundays. That's the one day I can't work. But any other day is fine.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: That's perfectly fine. Sunday is not a normal workday here. So full-time, Monday to Friday, 6 to 2:30. Does that sound good?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: Yes, that sounds great. I'm ready to start as soon as possible.

drills.title: Can / Can't for Availability
drills.instruction: Say whether you are available or not. Use: I can / I can't work + [time or day]
examples: I can work weekdays from 6 to 3.
I can't work nights — I have children at home.
She can work part-time on weekdays.
He can't start before 8 AM.
Can you work the early morning shift?
drills.your_turn: Can you work the early morning shift?

drills.title: Time Prepositions: On, At, From...To
drills.instruction: Fill in the correct preposition: on, at, from, to, or until.

prompts.sentence: I can stay ___ 6 PM if needed.

examples: I work on weekdays.
The store opens at 9 AM.
My shift is from 7 to 3.
I work until the job is done.
I'm available on weekends too.

drills.title: Schedule Questions
drills.instruction: Ask about schedule information. Use the question words and phrases you learned.

prompts.sentence: ___ are the hours for this job?
Do you offer ___ or part-time work?

examples: What are the hours for this position?
What shift would I work — morning or afternoon?
Is overtime available at this company?
Do you offer full-time or part-time?
How many hours per week is this job?
drills.your_turn: How many hours per week is this job?

listening.question: What are the work hours for the job in the audio?
options: Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM
Monday to Saturday, 7 AM to 3 PM
Monday to Friday, 6 AM to 2:30 PM
Tuesday to Saturday, 9 AM to 6 PM
listening.explanation: The hiring manager says 'The shift is Monday through Friday, from 6 AM to 2:30 PM.' Listening carefully for 'from...to' helps you catch exact times.

listening.question: What does the woman say about weekends?
options: She can work both Saturday and Sunday
She can work Saturdays but not Sundays
She can't work any weekends
She works every Sunday
listening.explanation: The woman says 'I'm available on Saturdays, but I can't work on Sundays.' This shows how to clearly separate your available and unavailable days.

listening.question: What does 'full-time' mean in the job description?
options: Working 20 hours per week
Working whenever the employer needs you
Working 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Working only on weekends
listening.explanation: The employer explains 'This is a full-time position — 40 hours a week, Monday through Friday.' Knowing this term helps you understand what you are applying for.

speaking.title: Your Availability
speaking.instruction: Record yourself explaining when you can and cannot work. Include: which days, which hours, and whether you can do overtime. Use: I can work..., I'm available..., I can't work...
speaking.example: I can work Monday through Friday. I'm available for morning or daytime shifts — from about 6 AM to 4 PM. I can also work on Saturdays if overtime is available. I can't work on Sundays. I prefer full-time work, but I can do part-time too.

speaking.title: Ask About the Schedule
speaking.instruction: Imagine you are calling about a job. Record yourself asking 3 questions about the schedule and hours. Use: What are the hours?, What shift...?, Is ... available?
speaking.example: Hello, I'm calling about the warehouse position. I have a few questions. What are the hours for this job? Is it full-time or part-time? And is overtime available? Thank you for your time.

writing.title: My Availability
writing.instruction: Write 4-5 sentences describing your work availability. Include: which days you can work, what hours you prefer, and at least one time you cannot work. Use: on, at, from...to, until.
writing.example: I am available to work Monday through Saturday. I can work from 6 AM to 4 PM on weekdays. On Saturdays, I am available until 2 PM. I cannot work on Sundays. I am looking for a full-time position, but I can start with part-time work.

writing.title: A Schedule Conversation
writing.instruction: Write a short conversation (4-6 lines) between a worker and an employer about schedule and hours. Include at least one question and one answer about availability.
writing.example:
Employer: The position is Monday to Friday, from 7 AM to 3:30 PM. Does that work for you?
Worker: Yes, that works well. I'm available every weekday.
Employer: Great. Would you be available for overtime on Saturdays?
Worker: Yes, I can work on Saturdays too. I'm not available on Sundays, but any other day is fine.

sections.title: ON, AT, FROM...TO — time prepositions for schedules
examples: I work on Mondays. ✓ (on + day of week)
I work at Monday. ✗ (don't use 'at' with days)
The shift starts at 6 AM. ✓ (at + specific time)
The shift starts on 6 AM. ✗
I work from 8 to 4. ✓ (from start to end)
I work from 8 until 4. ✓ (until = same as 'to')
I'm available on weekdays. ✓ (weekdays = Monday–Friday)
sections.question: When do we use ON vs AT vs FROM...TO?
sections.explanation: Use ON with days of the week (on Monday, on weekends). Use AT with specific clock times (at 6 AM, at noon). Use FROM...TO or FROM...UNTIL for ranges (from 8 to 4, from Monday to Friday). Never mix them: 'at Monday' or 'on 6 AM' are mistakes.

sections.title: Full-time, Part-time, Shift, Overtime — important work schedule words
examples: Full-time = 40 hours per week (usually Monday–Friday)
Part-time = fewer than 40 hours (can vary)
Shift = a set block of work time (morning shift: 6–2, afternoon shift: 2–10, night shift: 10–6)
Overtime = hours worked beyond your regular schedule (often paid more)
Off = not working (I'm off on Sundays. Today is my day off.)
sections.question: What is the difference between a shift and overtime?
sections.explanation: A shift is your regular scheduled work period. Overtime is extra time worked beyond your regular hours — often on a day off or after your shift ends. Overtime is usually paid at a higher rate. Knowing these words will help you understand job postings and conversations with employers.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses a time preposition?
options: I work on 8 AM every day.
I work at Mondays.
I work from 7 AM to 3 PM.
I work to Monday and Friday.
quiz.explanation: 'From 7 AM to 3 PM' is correct — FROM...TO is used for time ranges. 'At' is for specific times (at 8 AM), 'on' is for days (on Mondays), not mixed with each other.

quiz.question: Ahmed says 'I can't work on Sundays.' What does this mean?
options: He doesn't want to work ever
Sunday is his only available day
Sunday is a day he is not available to work
He works every Sunday
quiz.explanation: 'I can't work on Sundays' means Sunday is not available for him. He can work other days. This is a natural and clear way to express your unavailability.

quiz.question: What is a 'shift'?
options: A type of overtime pay
A scheduled block of work time (e.g., 6 AM to 2:30 PM)
A day off from work
A full week of work
quiz.explanation: A shift is a specific scheduled period of work time — for example, a morning shift from 6 to 2:30 or a night shift from 10 PM to 6 AM. Most warehouses and factories work in shifts.

quiz.question: How do you ask about work hours in a job interview?
options: When do I have to come?
What are the hours for this position?
Tell me the schedule now.
Is the job in the morning?
quiz.explanation: 'What are the hours for this position?' is professional and natural. It shows you are thinking about the schedule and taking the job seriously.

quiz.question: Tom offers Saturday overtime. How does Ahmed correctly say he can do it?
options: I'm available on Saturdays.
I available Saturday.
Saturday I can available.
I work Saturday, yes.
quiz.explanation: 'I'm available on Saturdays' is the natural, correct form. Use 'available + on + day' to express your availability.

quiz.question: What does 'full-time' typically mean?
options: Working only in the morning
Working whenever the boss calls you
Working about 40 hours per week
Working 7 days a week
quiz.explanation: Full-time usually means 40 hours per week, typically Monday through Friday. Part-time means fewer hours — often 20-30 hours per week.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses UNTIL?
options: I work until Monday.
I work until at 5 PM.
I can stay until 6 PM if needed.
The shift is until from 8 to 4.
quiz.explanation: 'I can stay until 6 PM' is correct. UNTIL is followed by a time or event. You can also say 'from 8 to 4' or 'from 8 until 4' — both work.

quiz.question: What is overtime?
options: A type of shift that starts very early
Work done beyond your regular scheduled hours
The time when your shift ends
A job that pays very well
quiz.explanation: Overtime is extra work time beyond your regular schedule — often on weekends or after your regular shift ends. It is usually optional and paid at a higher rate.

quiz.question: Write 3 sentences about your work availability. Use: I can work..., I'm available..., I can't...
quiz.explanation: Practice stating your availability clearly. Include days, hours, and at least one limitation. This is essential information for any job interview.

quiz.question: An employer asks: 'What shift do you prefer — morning, afternoon, or night?' Write your answer in 2 sentences. Explain your preference and why.
quiz.explanation: Employers appreciate when you know your own availability. Be honest and specific. Example: 'I prefer the morning shift, from 6 to 2. I am more productive in the morning and it fits my family schedule.'
